description:
Wire the helper's length-prefixed JSON-RPC 2.0 transport and the protocol-type definitions per N-007 §§4–7. No business logic in the methods yet — every method returns a sentinel "not implemented" error so the transport can be exercised end-to-end without any subsystem behind it.

Scope (binding):
- Implement the length-prefixed JSON-RPC 2.0 framing exactly per N-007 §4.2:
  - 4-byte big-endian length header, then UTF-8 JSON-RPC payload.
  - 1 MiB max frame size; oversized frames refused with JSON-RPC `error.code = -32600`.
  - Requests, responses, and notifications all carry the standard JSON-RPC envelope.
- Transport listener:
  - Linux/macOS: bind a Unix domain socket at the path passed via `--ipc-socket`. `umask` set so the socket is `0600` (owner rw only).
  - Windows: bind a named pipe at the path passed via `--ipc-socket` with per-user ACL. Windows support is shape-only — pulling in `tokio::net::windows::named_pipe` is sufficient; a feature flag is acceptable.
  - Single-connection model: at most one client (the Electron main process) is connected at a time. A second connect attempt is refused with an immediate close.
  - On `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM`, drain in-flight responses with a 2 s deadline then close.
- Method dispatcher:
  - Stub implementations for every method listed in N-007 §5: `capture.listSources`, `capture.requestSession`, `capture.startStream`, `capture.pauseStream`, `capture.resumeStream`, `capture.stopSession`, `capture.setRegion`, `capture.setFramerateHint`, `capture.setCursorMode`, `replay.save`, `replay.snapshot_release`, `replay.recoverable_sessions`, `replay.discard_recovered_session`, `replay.restore_recovered_session`, `replay.export_start`, `replay.export_cancel`, `engine.version`, `engine.health`, `engine.setLogLevel`, `engine.shutdown`, `engine.diagnosticsBundlePath`.
  - Every stub returns JSON-RPC error `{ code: "not-implemented", message: "<method>: stub" }` EXCEPT:
    - `engine.version` returns `{ helperVersion: HELPER_VERSION, protocolVersion: PROTOCOL_VERSION }`.
    - `engine.setLogLevel` actually adjusts the `tracing_subscriber` filter.
    - `engine.shutdown` initiates a graceful shutdown of the transport.
- Protocol type definitions:
  - All Serde structs/enums from N-007 §7 declared in `protocol::types`: `CaptureMode`, `CursorMode`, `Rect`, `RequestSessionOpts`, `CaptureSourceDescriptor`, `CaptureFormat`, `SessionReadyEvent`, `ReplaySnapshot`, `SegmentRef`, `RecoverableSession`, `AudioMode`, `ExportOptions`, `PlanReport`, `EngineState`, `EngineStatus`, `EngineHealth`, plus the event payloads from N-007 §6.
  - Wire format snake_case (per N-007 §7 prose); use `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` on enums and `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` is NOT used — main process re-keys to camelCase per the design.
- Event emission helper: a `Notifier` handle that subsystems will later call to push notifications to the client. In this ticket, no subsystem emits anything except a single `engine.ready { helperVersion, protocolVersion, pid, capabilities: [] }` notification fired immediately after the client connects.
- Connect logging: every connect/disconnect logged at `info`; every method call logged at `debug` with method name + request id.

Out of scope (binding):
- No Electron-side client (T-013).
- No real `capture.*`, `replay.*`, `export.*` logic beyond the stub error (T-016..T-019).
- No PID file management (that lives in `engine.*` and is handled jointly with T-013).
- No restart loop / supervisor logic — this ticket only exposes a transport; supervision lives on the Electron side (T-013).
- No actual TypeScript bindings in `electron/` or `src/` — types only exist in the helper. T-013/T-014 introduce the TS counterparts.
- Helper SHA-256 sidecar / boot-time verification — that is part of T-013 main-side wiring + T-010d packaging.

Acceptance criteria:
1. `cargo test -p cove-replay-engine` passes a round-trip test: a Tokio test connects to an in-process listener, sends `{ "jsonrpc":"2.0", "id":1, "method":"engine.version", "params":null }`, and receives a well-formed response with `helperVersion` and `protocolVersion`.
2. The transport rejects a malformed frame (length-prefix says 2 MiB) with JSON-RPC `error.code = -32600` and does not crash.
3. `engine.shutdown` causes the listener to stop accepting new connections within 100 ms; in-flight responses still deliver.
4. `engine.setLogLevel { level: "debug" }` toggles the subscriber filter (verified by a tracing test layer or by reading the rolling log).
5. Every method from N-007 §5 is dispatchable; stubs return a `not-implemented` error with the method name in the message.
6. `engine.ready` notification fires within 50 ms of client connect (verified by the round-trip test).
7. No method ever causes a panic; all errors are returned as JSON-RPC error responses.

Verification commands:
- `cargo build -p cove-replay-engine`
- `cargo test -p cove-replay-engine`
- Manual: `./target/debug/cove-replay-engine --ipc-socket /tmp/test.sock --log-dir /tmp --log-level debug &`; `socat - UNIX-CONNECT:/tmp/test.sock` and send a hand-crafted length-prefixed JSON-RPC request (operator may script this, not gated).
- `git status --short`

Codex review expectations:
- Verify the length-prefix is exactly 4 bytes big-endian per N-007 §4.2 (a common bug is little-endian).
- Verify the 1 MiB cap exists and is enforced before any allocation of the payload buffer (no allocation amplification attack).
- Verify Serde rename rules match the wire format documented in N-007 §7.
- Confirm no subsystem types (capture / encoder / segment / export) leaked into the transport layer.
- Confirm no PipeWire / ffmpeg dependencies were added.
- Flag any deviation from the method signatures in N-007 §5.

Failure handling:
- If `tokio::net::windows::named_pipe` cross-platform feature flagging causes pain, gate the Windows path behind `#[cfg(target_os = "windows")]` and leave a one-line `compile_error!` stub note in the helper. v2.0.0 ships Linux first (N-008 §4).

No commits, tags, or publishes from this ticket.
title: Implement helper JSON-RPC transport and protocol types
